Medication List for Patient P1001

Patient: Alex Morgan (fictional — all data synthetic)
Patient ID: P1001
Medications as of Discharge Date: 2024-01-20

This document contains the complete discharge medication list for patient P1001. All entries are synthetic and for system testing purposes only.

Medications:

1. Name: Warfarin
   Dose: 5 mg
   Frequency: Once daily, in the evening
   Route: Oral
   Indication: Prevention of deep vein thrombosis following total knee replacement
   Instructions: Take at the same time each day. INR monitoring is required. Avoid NSAIDs (including ibuprofen and naproxen) while taking warfarin, as the combination significantly increases bleeding risk. Avoid significant changes in dietary vitamin K intake.
   Prescriber: Dr. Patricia Holloway (fictional)

2. Name: Ibuprofen
   Dose: 400 mg
   Frequency: Three times daily as needed for breakthrough pain
   Route: Oral
   Indication: Pain and inflammation management
   Instructions: Take with food. NOTE — This medication has a known interaction with warfarin (also on this medication list). The combination of warfarin and ibuprofen significantly increases the risk of serious bleeding. This entry is retained in this record as a clinical documentation artifact from a prior prescription. Discuss with your physician before taking ibuprofen while on warfarin.
   Prescriber: Dr. Samuel Reeves (fictional)

3. Name: Oxycodone/Acetaminophen
   Dose: 5 mg / 325 mg
   Frequency: Every 4 to 6 hours as needed for moderate to severe pain
   Route: Oral
   Indication: Post-surgical pain management
   Instructions: Do not exceed 6 tablets per day. Do not take with additional acetaminophen-containing products. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medication. May cause drowsiness and constipation.
   Prescriber: Dr. Patricia Holloway (fictional)

4. Name: warfarin
   Dose: 5 mg
   Frequency: Once daily
   Route: Oral
   Indication: Anticoagulation — duplicate entry from pre-operative medication reconciliation record
   Instructions: This entry is a duplicate of medication #1 above (warfarin 5 mg daily). It is retained here as a documentation artifact from the pre-operative medication reconciliation. A duplicate entry warning should be generated, as two entries exist for warfarin (case-insensitive match: 'Warfarin' and 'warfarin').
   Prescriber: Dr. Samuel Reeves (fictional)

5. Name: Acetaminophen
   Dose: 500 mg
   Frequency: Every 6 hours scheduled
   Route: Oral
   Indication: Baseline pain management (scheduled, not as-needed)
   Instructions: Do not exceed 3,000 mg of acetaminophen from all sources per day. Combine carefully with the oxycodone/acetaminophen combination product to avoid exceeding the daily acetaminophen limit.
   Prescriber: Dr. Patricia Holloway (fictional)

6. Name: Pantoprazole
   Dose: 40 mg
   Frequency: Once daily, before breakfast
   Route: Oral
   Indication: Gastrointestinal protection during post-surgical recovery period
   Instructions: Take 30 minutes before eating. Reduces stomach acid to protect the stomach lining.
   Prescriber: Dr. Patricia Holloway (fictional)

7. Name: Docusate Sodium
   Dose: 100 mg
   Frequency: Twice daily
   Route: Oral
   Indication: Stool softener — prevention of opioid-induced constipation
   Instructions: Take with a full glass of water. Increase fluid intake while using this medication.
   Prescriber: Dr. Patricia Holloway (fictional)

Allergies on File: Penicillin (reaction: rash — documented 2019)

Known Interaction Alert:
Warfarin + Ibuprofen — HIGH severity interaction. Both medications are present in this patient's medication list. The combination of warfarin and ibuprofen significantly increases the risk of serious and potentially life-threatening bleeding events. This interaction must be reviewed with the prescribing physician before ibuprofen is administered.

Duplicate Medication Alert:
Warfarin appears twice in this medication list (entries #1 and #4), with names differing only in case ('Warfarin' and 'warfarin'). This duplicate entry was identified during medication reconciliation and is flagged for pharmacist review and resolution.
